source_text: Καὶ ἱκανά γε νομίζω ταῦτα εἶναι τῷ βουλομένῳ παραστῆσαι τὴν Ἰουδαίων πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπιστίαν, ὅτι ἀκόλουθος ἦν αὕτη τοῖς ἐξ ἀρχῆς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀναγεγραμμένοις. εἴποιμι γὰρ ἂν πρὸς τὸν λέγοντα παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖον· τίς θεὸς παρὼν εἰς ἀνθρώπους ἀπιστεῖται, καὶ ταῦτα οἷς ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπιφαίνεται; ἢ τί δή ποτε τοῖς πάλαι προσδεχομένοις οὐ γνωρίζεται; ὅτι βούλεσθε, ὦ οὗτοι, πρὸς τὰς πεύσεις ἡμῶν ἀποκρίνεσθαι; ποῖαι δυνάμεις μείζους ὅσον ἐπὶ ὑμετέρᾳ ὑπολήψει εἶναι ὑμῖν φαίνονται, αἱ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἢ ἃ ἔφαμεν ἡμεῖς πεποιηκέναι τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν; εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἐκεῖναι μείζους τούτων καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς εἰσιν, πῶς οὐκ αὐτόθεν δείκνυται ὅτι κατὰ τὸ ἦθος τῶν τοῖς μείζοσιν ἀπιστησάντων ἐστὶ καὶ τὸ τῶν ἡττόνων καταφρονεῖν; τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπολαμβάνεται περὶ ὧν λέγομεν περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ· εἰ δὲ ἴσαι λέγονται (αἱ) περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ταῖς ἀναγεγραμμέναις ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως, τί ξένον ἀπήντησε λαῷ κατ᾿ ἀμφοτέρας τὰς ἀρχὰς τῶν πραγμάτων ἀπιστοῦντι; ἀρχὴ μὲν γὰρ νομοθεσίας ἐπὶ Μωϋσέως ἦν, ἐν ᾗ τὰ ἁμαρτήματα τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων ὑμῶν ἀναγέγραπται· ἀρχὴ δὲ νομοθεσίας καὶ διαθήκης δευτέρας κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἡμῖν γεγονέναι ὁμολογεῖται. καὶ μαρτυρεῖτε δι᾿ ὧν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπιστεῖτε ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἀπιστησάντων ταῖς θείαις ἐπιφανείαις· καὶ τὸ ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν εἰρημένον καὶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς λελέξεται ἀπιστήσαντας αὐτῷ, ὅτι „ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν“· καὶ πληροῦται ἐν ὑμῖν ἡ λέγουσα προφητεία· „ἔσται ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν κρεμαμένη ἐνώπιον τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε τῇ ζωῇ ὑμῶν“· οὐ γὰρ ἐπιστεύσατε τῇ ἐπιδεδημηκυίᾳ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ζωῇ.
pass_a_gloss: And sufficient (ἱκανός) I think these things to be for the one wishing to show (παρίστημι) the unbelief (ἀπιστία) of Jews toward Jesus, that it was consequent (ἀκόλουθος) to the things recorded from the beginning (ἐξ ἀρχῆς) about the people (λαός). For I would say toward the Jew speaking in Celsus: 'What god being present among men is disbelieved, and that (καὶ ταῦτα) appearing (ἐπιφαίνομαι) to those who hope (ἐλπίζω)? Or why ever (τί δή ποτε) is he not recognized (γνωρίζω) by those long (πάλαι) expecting (προσδέχομαι)?' — that: 'Are you willing (βούλομαι), O you (ὦ οὗτοι), to answer (ἀποκρίνομαι) toward our questions (πεῦσις)? What sort of powers/mighty works (δύναμις) appear to you greater (μείζων), so far as on your own supposition (ὑπόληψις): those in Egypt and the desert, or the things which we said Jesus did among (παρά) you? For if those are greater than these according to you, how is it not straightway (αὐτόθεν) shown (δείκνυμι) that according to the character (ἦθος) of those who disbelieved the greater is also the despising (καταφρονέω) of the lesser (ἥττων)? For this is supposed (ὑπολαμβάνω) about the things we say about Jesus. But if the [works] about Jesus are said equal (ἴσος) to those recorded by Moses, what strange thing (ξένον) has befallen (ἀπαντάω) a people disbelieving at both the beginnings (ἀρχή) of the affairs/dispensations (πράγματα)? For a beginning of legislation (νομοθεσία) was in the time of (ἐπί) Moses, in which the sins (ἁμάρτημα) of the unbelieving (ἄπιστος) and sinning of you have been recorded; and a beginning of legislation and of a second covenant (διαθήκη δευτέρα) is agreed/confessed (ὁμολογέω) by us to have come about according to (κατά) Jesus. And you bear witness (μαρτυρέω) through the things by which you disbelieve Jesus that you are sons (υἱός) of those in the desert who disbelieved the divine manifestations (θεία ἐπιφάνεια); and the thing said by our Savior (σωτήρ) will be said also toward you who disbelieved him, that: 'So (ἄρα) you are witnesses (μάρτυς) and approve-with (συνευδοκέω) the works (ἔργον) of your fathers'; and fulfilled (πληρόω) in you is the prophecy (προφητεία) saying: 'Your life (ζωή) will be hanging (κρεμάννυμι) before (ἐνώπιον) your eyes, and you will not at all (οὐ μή) believe your life'; for you did not believe the life that had sojourned (ἐπιδημέω, pf. ptc.) with the race (γένος) of men.
pass_b_english: And I think this is enough for anyone who wishes to show that the unbelief of the Jews toward Jesus was consistent with what was recorded about the people from the beginning. For to the Jew in Celsus who says, “What god, when present among men, is disbelieved, and that when he appears to those who are hoping for him? Or why ever is he not recognized by those who have long been expecting him?”, I would say this: Are you willing, sirs, to answer our questions? Which mighty works seem greater to you, so far as your own judgment goes: those in Egypt and in the wilderness, or those which we said Jesus did among you? If in your view those are greater than these, is it not plain at once that despising the lesser also fits the character of those who disbelieved the greater? For this is what is supposed about the things we tell of Jesus.

But if the mighty works told of Jesus are said to be equal to those recorded by Moses, what is strange in what has happened to a people that disbelieved at the beginning of both orders of things? For the beginning of the giving of the law came in the time of Moses, and in it the sins of the unbelievers and the sinners among you are recorded; and we acknowledge that the beginning of a second giving of law and of a second covenant came about with Jesus. And by your unbelief toward Jesus you bear witness that you are sons of those who in the wilderness disbelieved the divine manifestations (compare Matthew 23:31). And what our Savior said will be said to you also, who disbelieved him: “So you are witnesses, and you approve the deeds of your fathers” (Luke 11:48). And in you the prophecy is fulfilled that says, “Your life will be hanging before your eyes, and you will not believe your life” (Deuteronomy 28:66). For you did not believe the Life that had come to dwell among the human race.

choices.why: Origen's imagined reply taken out of double quotation marks (house style keeps them for Celsus and Scripture); inner Scripture quotations back to double marks
'Will you be willing' made 'Are you willing' (present βούλεσθε)
'what was written about the people' made 'what was recorded' (ἀναγεγραμμένοις)
'the works told of Jesus' made 'the mighty works' to match δυνάμεις

'what strange thing has befallen a people that disbelieved at both beginnings of these dispensations' made 'what is strange in what has happened to a people that disbelieved at the beginning of both orders of things' (rhetorical τί ξένον; 'these' and 'dispensations' were additions for πραγμάτων)
'is confessed by us to have come in Jesus' made 'we acknowledge ... came about with Jesus' (κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν parallel to ἐπὶ Μωϋσέως)

translator_notes: Celsus’s question (‘What god... long been expecting him?’) is in double quotation marks. Origen’s imagined reply to the Jew runs from ‘Are you willing, sirs’ to the end; it is left unquoted, introduced by ‘I would say this:’, so that double quotation marks stay reserved for Celsus’s words and Scripture. ὅτι before βούλεσθε is taken as introducing direct speech (it could be a corrupt τί, ‘What will you answer...?’). ὦ οὗτοι, a direct, slightly brusque address, rendered ‘sirs’. τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπολαμβάνεται (‘this is supposed’) is impersonal: the Jews suppose Jesus’ works to be the lesser; kept impersonal. τί ξένον ἀπήντησε is a rhetorical question expecting ‘nothing’; rendered ‘what is strange in what has happened’. κατ᾿ ἀμφοτέρας τὰς ἀρχὰς τῶν πραγμάτων rendered ‘at the beginning of both orders of things’ (the Mosaic lawgiving and the new covenant). ἡμῖν with ὁμολογεῖται taken as ‘by us’ (‘we acknowledge’); κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν, parallel to ἐπὶ Μωϋσέως, rendered ‘with Jesus’. ‘Sons of those who...’ echoes Matthew 23:31 (μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας), marked ‘compare’. Luke 11:48 is quoted exactly. Deuteronomy 28:66 LXX has the singular (ἡ ζωή σου... ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου... καὶ οὐ πιστεύσεις τῇ ζωῇ σου); Origen gives plurals, ἐνώπιον and οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε; rendered as he quotes it. The verse was read in the early Church as a prophecy of Christ hanging on the cross, and Origen’s last sentence plays on it; ‘Life’ is capitalised there because it names Christ, while the quoted verse keeps lowercase ‘life’ so that the play stays visible.
